items.why: Launch entry price fell from $75 to $49 per month and the annual discount no longer applies to Launch.

record.short: Launch now starts at $49/mo, down from $75/mo; the up to 35% annual discount now covers only Growth and Scale.
record.headline: Baremetrics cut the starting price of its Launch plan from $75 to $49 per month and dropped the annual discount on that plan.
record.who: Businesses up to $360K ARR on the Launch plan; monthly payers gain most.
record.read: The old $75 monthly price with a 35% annual discount is replaced by a single $49 price, which looks like a simplification aimed at winning small founders. Annual payers on Launch likely see little change.
record.caveat: The prior annual price on Launch is not shown on the page, so the effect on annual payers is inferred.

Early Stage startup discount reduced from up to 96% to up to 93%; the example price with Early Stage rose from $30/mo to $65/mo.

record.short: Intercom’s Early Stage startup discount fell from 96% to 93% and the example Essential price with it rose from $30/mo to $65/mo.
record.headline: Intercom shrank its Early Stage startup discount from 96% to 93% and its worked example now shows $65/mo instead of $30/mo.
rows: Example total with Early Stage, per month
record.who: Startups under $10M raised and 15 employees or fewer applying to Early Stage.
record.read: A smaller startup discount means a higher effective entry cost for early customers. The 1 year of Fin free benefit is still advertised.
record.caveat: The $30 → $65 figure comes from the page’s pricing calculator example and may depend on the inputs shown (the list total of $109.09/mo did not change).

items.why: Hourly GPU prices for B300 and B200 rose on both Pods and Serverless.

record.short: B300 Pods rose from $8.99/hr to $10.49/hr and B200 Pods from $7.99/hr to $8.99/hr; Serverless rates rose similarly.
record.headline: Runpod raised hourly prices on its newest B300 and B200 GPUs across Pods and Serverless.
record.who: Anyone renting B300 or B200 GPUs; other GPU prices on the page were unchanged.
record.read: Increases on only the newest high-demand GPUs suggest a response to tight supply rather than a general repricing.
record.caveat: The Pods table shows one price per GPU in the captured text, so which cloud tier (Community or Secure) it refers to is unclear.
